tldr: The paper introduces the TEA protocol, which unifies tools, environments, and agents as versioned, lifecycle-managed components, and builds AGENTORCHESTRA, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that achieves 89.04% on GAIA Test and state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks.
contributions: Introduction of the TEA protocol that unifies environments, agents, and tools as first-class, versioned components with lifecycles for context management and execution
Development of AGENTORCHESTRA, a hierarchical multi-agent system built on TEA with tree-structured routing and feedback-driven self-evolution
Extensive evaluations on four benchmarks (GAIA, HLE, AIME, GPQA-Diamond) with ablations isolating key components
methods: The authors propose the TEA protocol, which defines three core context protocols—Tool Context Protocol (TCP), Environment Context Protocol (ECP), and Agent Context Protocol (ACP)—each with a context manager for lifecycle engineering and a server for standardized orchestration. Six protocol transformations (A2T, T2A, E2T, T2E, A2E, E2A) enable dynamic role reconfiguration across components. On top of TEA, AGENTORCHESTRA uses a central planning agent that decomposes user objectives and delegates to five specialized sub-agents (Deep Researcher, Browser Use, Deep Analyzer, Tool Generator, Reporter). A Self-Evolution Module optimizes prompts and execution solutions via textgrad and self-reflection, registering improved versions through the version manager.
results: AGENTORCHESTRA Evolved achieves 89.04% average accuracy on the GAIA Test set and 93.33% on the GAIA Validation set, outperforming strong baselines such as agent-2030 and Alita (87.27%). It reaches 85.53% on GAIA Level 2 and 81.63% on Level 3. The improvement from Vanilla to Evolved is largest on Validation Level 2 (+5.26 points). Evaluations also span HLE, AIME, and GPQA-Diamond across five model backbones (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, claude-sonnet-4.5, grok-4.1-fast, gemini-3-flash-preview).
limitations: The paper text is truncated and does not explicitly state limitations; however, the framework's reliance on specialized sub-agents and a central planner may introduce coordination overhead, and the self-evolution module's effectiveness is primarily demonstrated on medium-to-hard coordination regimes rather than simpler instances.
